Request changes: two holes remain in U2's totality/refusal guarantees, plus an identity gap in SL-327's cache repair.\n\n[P1] Run the undriven-closure refusal even when no frame ledger is built.\nsawc/coro_transform.py:12460-12461; _refuse_undriven_suspending_closures is called only later, at :12862.\nThe new closure refusal is still conditional on a coroutine root existing. _build_frame_ledger returns None when there are no driven/spawned roots and main does not own a framing cause; transform_program returns before the closure scan. This is precisely relevant to the imported helper whose enclosing function carries only a conservative cause.\n\nReproduced using the patch's own sl316closure fixture:\n  import sl316closure.{each_yield_public}\n  func main() {\n      let values: Vector<Int> = [1, 2]\n      print(each_yield_public(&values))\n  }\nCompile with --module-path sl316closure=examples/modules/sl316closure: succeeds and prints 2 despite the yield_now() inside the imported closure. Add an unrelated marker() containing __saw_suspend() and print(__saw_drive_steps(marker())) to main: the same imported closure is now correctly refused at lib.saw:23:17. Whether the unsupported closure is rejected must not depend on an unrelated drive site. Make the closure/effect validation available independently of frame construction and add the no-driven-root counterpart to the existing refusal test. This is an unclosed SL-316 cell, not a request to support suspending closures.\n\n[P1] Check genuine method calls in post-lowering totality.\nsawc/coro_transform.py:11589-11602.\nThe MethodCall loop asks ledger.key_of(mc), which intentionally returns None for a genuine method, and then checks only is_chan_recv. It never asks for the method's recorded suspension/target. Consequently a plain instance/static method call left in a generated resume body is invisible to check (b).\n\nIndependent fault injection on examples/coro_nested_suspend_method.saw: captured the real typed c.step() node before lowering and inserted a copy into a generated resume body immediately before _verify_resume_totality. The frozen ledger answered MethodTarget(kind='embed', frame_key='Counter_step', owner='Counter', is_static=False), and key_of returned None. _verify_resume_totality returned successfully. The probe removed the injected node afterward so the control compiler could finish; this establishes that the invariant misses the injected method call, not that the subsequent re-typecheck accepts it. The committed gate exercises only a free FunctionCall, so it passes despite this gap.\n\nRoute genuine methods through the ledger's appropriate method decision, distinguishing synthesized resume/release/runtime calls, and add method-family negative controls beside the free-call injection (instance, static and generic/stamped where applicable). The promised post-lowering guarantee covers all frame-boundary calls, not just free/module-qualified calls and channel receives.\n\n[P2] Validate cached seed identity, not numeric-ID membership alone.\nsawc/stdcache.py:210-215; sawc/sawc.py:805-810.\n_pair_is_consistent accepts a seed key whenever that integer exists among AST methods. _rekeyed_std_seed has the same fast path and preserves an existing integer unconditionally. But the defect being repaired is that the table and AST can belong to different node-ID generations: an integer can name the WRONG method as well as no method. The code already builds by_id -> (owner, name), but never compares that identity with the seed entry.\n\nDirect synthetic pairing probe: AST Command.output has node_id 20 and Command.status has node_id 10; the stale seed table has key 10 and display identity `Command.output`. _pair_is_consistent returns True and _rekeyed_std_seed returns the table unchanged, leaving output unseeded and attributing its causes to status. This is a fault-injection test of the repair boundary; I did not find such a colliding blob on this machine. Check identity before trusting a surviving integer, re-key mismatches using a stable identity, and gate both missing-ID and wrong-method-ID cases. Also make unresolvable seed identities trigger an explicit cache fallback/invariant rather than silently dropping their entries.\n\nValidation: independently ran corototality and corodiscovery (both pass), plus seven focused runtime/refusal tests (7/7: K118, qualified generic embedding, entry-template chain, generic expression call, existential-only framing, imported suspending closure, paired thread diagnostics). Ran the additional probes above and git diff --check (clean). Full battery GREEN, **32/32 stages** (3720s) — the 32nd is a new lane this unit owed. Awaiting the lead's validation + patch (SL-318.p7).\n\n- `04ec6faf` the statement-scoped window, the borrowing struct, and the two missing splits\n- `c420e372` the conformance rows K132-K149, and the two release paths the fixtures found\n- `1140a99e` docs for the borrowing struct, the `for` window and the two splits\n- `f2927e67` the four battery lanes the unit owed\n- `0230727d` the `windowseam` lane — the reuse obligation, gated\n\nGate counts: suite **2615 passed / 14 xfailed**; freestanding **36/36** (riscv32 + arm64); battery **32/32**. Conformance subset **354 passed / 2 xfailed**; SL-333's pins **37 passed**, unchanged. No existing `examples/conformance/K*.saw` file was edited — only `INDEX.md`.\n\n---\n\n## 1. The window record and its chokepoint\n\n`sawc/windows.py`. ONE record, `StatementWindow`: root path, root binding id, mode, origin, the EXTENT statement, the client, and a GENERIC resource slot (`resource_name` / `resource_type`) — never a field named `__iter`, never an `Iterator`-shaped payload. ONE chokepoint, `WindowTable`, whose docstring names its clients.\n\n**Clients** — `for` is the only one in U3 (`typechecker/borrowing.py::open_for_window` / `close_for_window`, called from `statements.py`'s two `for` checkers); the reserved second is the generic scoped-borrow statement, filed as SL-342.\n\n**Entries the chokepoint owns**, so no client does them twice:\n- the ROOT CHARGE, read at the four access sites design 189's task-capture extent already had — a name read (`expressions._check_identifier`), a `move` (`_check_move_expr`), a CALL's access set (`types._check_call_exclusivity`, which is where `v.push`, a `&var` argument, an `o.take()` receiver, a closure's borrow captures and a design-201 spawn argument all arrive) and a WRITE target (`statements._check_write_target`);\n- the EXCLUSIVITY conflicts, including a `&var` extent live at the head or STARTED in the body;\n- the MOVE / REASSIGN / TAKE / SWAP refusals on the root and on every enclosing owner;\n- the CLOSE-ON-EVERY-ROUTE accounting by RESOLVED CONTROL-FLOW TARGET. `windows_left_by(target_extents)` takes the extents the edge's target is still inside and answers inside-out — so `continue` targeting THIS loop keeps its window, `break` closes it, a jump targeting an INNER loop closes nothing of the outer, a window nested in an outer loop closes when control continues that outer loop, and `return`/error/cancellation pass the empty set. There is no `Continue` special case.\n\n**The record is a plain class, not a dataclass**, and the docstring says why: `typechecker/effects.py:substitute_ast_types` walks `dataclasses.fields()` and recurses into every dataclass VALUE, so a record whose `extent` points back at the statement holding it is a cycle the monomorphization walk descends until the recursion limit. Found by RecursionError on the first generic-collection fixture.\n\n**E8**, a named post-transform exemption beside design 218a §6's four: the window rule is about the AUTHORED program and ran on the authored tree one pass earlier. In a TRANSFORMED body `self` IS the frame — the collection has become `self.<field>` and every resume hand-off passes `&var self` — so the whole frame overlaps the window's root by the ordinary prefix rule. It covers the FENCE in both halves for the same reason: the transform's own lowering IS exception e2 (the resource becomes a `Slot<It>` frame field in a driven body, a `let` in a sync one), and judging the compiler's tree by the rule would be judging the answer by the question.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The borrowing struct\n\n`sawc/typechecker/borrowing.py`. Four spellings, each enforced:\n\n| spelling | rule | refusal row |\n|---|---|---|\n| `borrows struct` | design 130's `unsafe struct` position; no name convention | `_error_borrows_prefix` for every other position |\n| `private v: &Vector<T, A>` | the ordinary reference spelling; the ONE exception to DF-163d, TOP-LEVEL and SHARED only | K145 (`&var` field), K143 (nested reference) |\n| `borrows -> S` | a VALUE-returning producer | K144 (missing `borrows`) |\n| `lends self` | the ONLY origin, `&self` receiver required | K144 (projection, foreign parameter, `&var self`) |\n\n`lends` is a **CONTEXTUAL keyword** (the `import`/`module`/`export` precedent), so neither lexer's table changes: `lexdiff`, `astdiff` and `selfhostlex` are untouched by the new word. `borrows struct` reuses the existing `BORROWS` token.\n\n**The lend/producer split is answerable before type checking.** `place_transform` runs ahead of the checker and cannot look up whether a return type names a `borrows struct` (it may be imported), so it splits on two facts it does have: the DECLARED return type is not a reference (SL-333 R1 made `-> &T` mean \"lend\" whatever the body does) and the body contains no `lend`. A `borrows -> T` body that DOES lend still gets R1's fixit; a `borrows -> &T` body with no `lend` still gets design 141's coverage error. The producer then gets `place_self_by_pointer` — the SAME bit DF-146b set for an accessor, not a second ABI — because a copy's address dies with the call.\n\n**R5's FIELD clause** was added to the sentence SL-333 wrote, in `parser/types.py:reject_reference_field` and in the spec, rather than a second sentence beside it.\n\n**The fence: one question at one line.** `check_borrowing_fence` is called from `_check_expression` where `resolved_type` is stamped — the one line every expression's type passes through — so the position list is a matrix of TESTS, not of checks. Four exceptions, each documented: e1 the producer's own construction and return; e2 the compiler's hidden binding (E8); e3 the struct's own extension methods' receiver; e4 the reference field, which AUTO-DEREFERENCES at member access exactly as a reference parameter does — which is what confines it to a non-escaping re-borrow with no second rule, since references are not first-class.\n\n**The rejector's rows.** Three phrases, and that is deliberate: the fence has no parent slot in hand, so the sentence that matters is the RULE. Two positions a CLIENT knows get their own diagnosis because the ACT differs.\n\n| row | position | message |\n|---|---|---|\n| K142.1-9 | `let`, `var`, argument, discarded statement, tuple element, collection-literal element, assignment RHS, closure return, `??` operand | ``may not be used outside a window head`` |\n| K142.10 | TEMPORARY receiver | ``may not be produced from a TEMPORARY receiver`` + \"bind the collection first\" |\n| K142.11 | head is an `if`/`match`/block/`try` EXPRESSION | ``may not be produced by an `if` / `match` / block / `try` expression in the head`` |\n| K143 | parameter, field, plain return, type argument, static, associated `Item` | ``may not name a borrowing struct`` — at the DECLARATION |\n| K144 | `lends self.items`, `lends other`, `&var self` receiver, a field not initialized with `lends self`, a `borrows struct` with no reference field | one message each, each naming the rule |\n| K145 | `&var T` field | ``may not be an EXCLUSIVE reference`` + the reallocation argument |\n\nA by-value receiver is NOT a row: the parser already refuses `self` without a sigil, so the origin rule's own refusal for it is unreachable from source.\n\n**std.** `VectorIterator<T, A>` and `EnumeratedIterator<T, A>` are the four-line shape holding `&Vector<T, A>`; `next()` reads `length` and `buffer` through the reference on every call and the only `unsafe` left is the index through the buffer. **`public` KEPT** on both, and the comment now says why: design 80's signature-visibility rule (a public `iter()` may not name a private type), NOT so a caller can hold one — holding is refused. The ALLOCATOR type parameter is new on both (the old shape held a bare `UnsafePointer<T>` and needed none, which is also why nothing connected the iterator to the vector).\n\n---\n\n## 3. The four matrix axes, per cell\n\n**ITERATOR × SUSPENSION POSITION × CONTEXT** — `K133_window_spans_a_suspension.saw`, 14 cells, each against its sync twin:\n\n| iterator | driven | spawned | embedded in spawned | nested in while | nested in for |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `Vector.iter` | 12 ok | 12 ok | 24 ok | 24 ok | 36 ok |\n| `Vector.enumerated` | 15 ok | — | — | — | — |\n| a USER borrowing iterator | 12 ok | — | — | — | — |\n| a RECORD-LESS user iterator (owns its source, opens NO window) | 12 ok | — | — | — | — |\n| `Map.keys` (owned copy — the control) | 6 ok | — | — | — | — |\n\nThe HEAD axis is K138's, where the ACQUIRE sequence is what it measures.\n\n**ROOT** — `K135`, all ok at 12: frame-local, `&` param, `&var` param of a driven callee, an ENCLOSING FRAME's field (`self.inner`), a field of a `&var self` receiver, a GENERIC collection instantiation (`Wrapper<Int>`). Every one is a persistent slot by the direct-head rule.\n\n**CONFLICT** — refusals in `errors/window_conflicts.saw` (one compile, 8 diagnostics): the body pushes; `with_var_ref` on the root; a `&var` extent STARTED in the body (a design-201 spawn argument); `move` of the root; reassignment of the root; `swap` of two elements; a write of the window's own root path through its owner (`st.patches = []`). The `while` one emits into the HEADER block, which every backedge and every `continue` re-enters, so the clear lands once per EVALUATION and a body that reinitializes the local keeps running: SL-226 review r1's rule, reached by the split path's own structure rather than by a second `_head_into_while_body`. `match` keeps `consuming=False` for the reason the in-place arm gives — a `match` consumes an owned scrutinee by construction, and a `move` there would cost the arm bindings their drop flags.\n\n**Sibling probe (obligation 4), every split container head, compile+run, driven, inside a spanning collection `for`:**\n\n| head | main | branch BEFORE | branch AFTER |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `if consume_bool(move r) { continue }` | 2 drops / 5 | REFUSED (`_split_if`) | 2 drops / 5 |\n| `while consume_bool(move r) { … }` (exit + reinit) | drop old → 3 / drop old, drop new → 6 | REFUSED (`_split_while`) | same as main |\n| `match consume_int(move r) { case 1 -> { continue } … }` | 2 drops / 6 | REFUSED (`_split_match`) | 2 drops / 6 |\n| `if let n = consume_opt(move r) { continue }` | 2 drops / 7 | 2 drops / 7 | 2 drops / 7 |\n| `guard let n = consume_opt(move r) else { continue }` | 2 drops / 8 | 2 drops / 8 | 2 drops / 8 |\n| `while let` subject | correct | correct | correct |\n| range `for` bounds | correct | correct | correct |\n\nThe `match` row is the sweep's find and the ruling's own argument applies to it unchanged: it **COMPILED AND RAN CORRECTLY ON MAIN** over a collection `for` and was refused on the branch, because `match_return` — the only `match` cell in the corpus — has an arm that `return`s and so needs no split at all. The three that already relinquish do it through a position the split path already had: the optional-binding dispatch runs the clears on BOTH branches, and `_split_for` stores its bounds ahead of the loop.\n\n## SL-339 — the try landing's ERROR edge\n\n`move r` hands ownership to the callee AT THE CALL, so the frame's claim is dead whichever way control leaves afterwards. A LEAF statement's lowering emits the drop-flag clear as a TRAILING statement — correct and sufficient for a straight-line edge, and where SL-234 put it — and `_emit_try_landing` then wraps the lowered sequence in a synthesized `try { <it> } catch { … }` whose error edge leaves before reaching it. **`_trailing_forgets` is the one funnel those clears go through now**; its docstring names every entry point (the `DestructuringLet` arm's two returns, `LetStatement`, `AssignStatement`'s two returns, the fallback, and `_done_seq` — the `ReturnStatement` arm's trailing position), and it records into an accumulator the two landing emitters install around their `_lower_inplace` call. `_emit_try_landing` re-emits them ahead of the error store; `_emit_try_propagate` hands them to `_done_seq`, which is where the frame's `release()` would otherwise destroy a second time what the callee already took. `_hoist_head_and_relinquish` is deliberately NOT an entry: a container's clear already sits on its head's own success edge, and re-running it on an error edge raised from a BLOCK would erase a claim that block re-established.\n\n**Sibling probe, compile+run, drop counts (one `Res` per iteration is correct):**\n\n| shape | main | branch AFTER |\n|---|---|---|\n| inline `try consume(move r) catch { break }` | 2 drops (double free) | 1 drop |\n| inline `try consume(move r) catch { continue }` | 4 drops | 2 drops |\n| BLOCK `try { … try consume(move r) … } catch { }` | 2 drops | 1 drop |\n| same, `let v = try consume_int(move r)` | 2 drops | 1 drop |\n| same, `n = try consume_int(move r)` | 2 drops | 1 drop |\n| same, OK edge (`try consume_ok(move r)`) | correct | correct |\n| no enclosing catch → `_emit_try_propagate` | 2 drops | 1 drop |\n| `return try consume_int(move r)` (`_done_seq`) | 2 drops | 1 drop |\n| `move` in the CATCH block | correct | correct |\n| `let _ = try? consume(move r)` (no landing built) | correct | correct |\n| CONTAINER head carrying both a `move` and a propagating `try` (`if (try consume_bool(move r)) { … }`, in-place and split) | 2 drops | 1 drop |\n\nThat last row is worth the ink: the design-120 ANF hoist lifts the propagating `try` to its own `let` first, so the shape arrives at the landing as a LEAF statement and the funnel covers it — verified against the branch tip `0230727d` as well as main, both of which double-freed it.\n\n**The ordering question that would have made this a design ruling, and why it is not one.** A statement whose propagating `try` errors BEFORE a sibling `move` is evaluated would owe NO relinquish on the error edge, and one landing cannot tell the two apart. It is unreachable: a BURIED propagating `try` (one sitting among siblings in an argument list or a binary operand) is refused today, identically on main and on the branch (``argument `value` expects `Bad` but got `Error` ``), so every `try` that reaches a landing is at the head of its statement's expression tree and every `move` in that statement has already happened. Probed both directions.\n\n## Markers, cells, files\n\n- The FOUR `// XFAIL: SL-33x` markers are gone, in the commit that fixes them.\n- `coro_head_move_relinquishes_before_early_exit.saw` — `try_break`, `try_continue`, `if_continue` and their EXPECT-OUTPUT lines restored **verbatim from main** (`git show main:… > …`), both MOVED-OUT comment blocks deleted.\n- `coro_head_move_with_early_exit_drops_once.saw` — I also restored the two DRIVEN `while` cells and their EXPECT lines, because the moved-out comment there cited \"XFAIL pins\" and would have gone stale; its sync/driven pairs are whole again. The `consume_vec` → `consume_text` change U3 made (the temporary-receiver fence) stands.\n- `coro_while_head_move_reevaluates_per_iteration.saw` — XFAIL paragraph dropped; the \"WHY EVERY CELL NESTS ITS `while` INSIDE A COLLECTION `for`\" paragraph now says the nesting is historical and no longer load-bearing, and that every driven cell takes `_split_while`'s lowering, which reads the same as the in-place arm.\n- The three pin files KEEP their names and cells as ordinary regression tests, headers rewritten to state the SPLIT-path rule and to say where the same bodies sit beside their sync twins. So the three restored cells are duplicated on purpose — say the word if you would rather have the pins deleted now that their homes are whole.\n- `coro_move_in_split_match_scrutinee.saw` is NEW: the sweep's row, which nothing in the corpus covered.\n- `coro_move_in_split_try_body.saw` gained four cells for the funnel's other entries (block spelling, `let`, the propagate edge, `return try`).\n- `sawc/coro_transform.py`'s `_normalize_inline_catch` docstring said the block form \"DOUBLE-FREES … SL-339 … pins it\"; it now records what closed it.\n- `designs/todo.md`: SL-338 and SL-339 closed in place inside U3's entry with the mechanism each fix targets. Tracker issues left for you.\n- `CLAUDE.md`: `windowseam` added to the `Stages:` list, after `corototality`, one parenthetical in the house style.\n\n## The value-position collection `for` (c71 §5, for the record)\n\n`let found = for x in v.iter() { if x > 1 { break x } }` with a NON-suspending body in a driven function compiled on main and printed `2`; on this branch it is refused with ``coroutine transform: suspending call to `yield_now` in `find` appears in a nested/expression position`` — the budget's synthesized yield named as a user call — which is byte-identical to what the RANGE `for` spelling already gives on main. [P1] Prove the origin of every returned borrowing value\nsawc/typechecker/borrowing.py:597-608\n\nThe producer check scans constructors anywhere in the body instead of following the values each returning path produces. One valid self-origin construction in the true arm makes the entire method pass, even when the other arm returns other.iter(). The call-site window then charges owner rather than other. The program below compiles/runs at exit 0 and prints 2 while assigning other.value inside that window; it must reject the foreign-origin return. Restrict the producer-body exemption and validate every returned value/path, not merely the existence and fields of constructors.\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { value: Int }\nborrows struct It { source: &Owner, done: Bool }\nextension Owner {\n func iter(&self) borrows -> It { It(source: lends self, done: false) }\n func bad(&self, other: &Owner, flag: Bool) borrows -> It {\n  if flag { It(source: lends self, done: false) } else { other.iter() }\n }\n}\nextension It: Iterator {\n type Item = Int\n func next(&var self) -> Int? {\n  if self.done { None } else {\n   self.done = true\n   self.source.value\n  }\n }\n}\nfunc main() {\n let owner = Owner(value: 1)\n var other = Owner(value: 2)\n for x in owner.bad(&other, false) {\n  other.value = 99\n  print(x)\n }\n}\n```\n\n2. [P1] Follow distinct aliases through the borrowing-type fence\nsawc/typechecker/borrowing.py:187-216; :246-261\n\nThe type walk does not follow the resolved distinct-alias target, and the value fence checks only the nominal borrowing struct. A borrowing iterator can therefore advertise Alias = It as its owned Item, yield Alias(self), and store that value in an outer optional after the window ends. Follow underlying aliases at declaration and value boundaries; the exemption for self inside iterator methods must not permit packaging the borrowing value for escape.\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { value: Int }\nborrows struct It { source: &Owner, done: Bool }\ntype Alias = It\nextension Owner {\n func iter(&self) borrows -> It { It(source: lends self, done: false) }\n}\nextension It: Iterator {\n type Item = Alias\n func next(&var self) -> Alias? {\n  if self.done { None } else {\n   self.done = true\n   Alias(self)\n  }\n }\n}\nfunc main() {\n let owner = Owner(value: 7)\n var saved: Alias? = None\n for x in owner.iter() { saved = x }\n print(saved.is_some())\n}\n```\n\n3. A runtime array index is not equal to a constant index, so bins[i] and bins[0] are considered disjoint even when i is 0. The following adjacent paths remain incorrect. Two independent Sol source reviews supplied candidates; I compiled/exercised the candidates below myself. Four non-borrow-syntax regressions were also run against exact base 82a6ab86.\n\n1. [P1] Copy-tier iterator heads are still bitwise loads, so the first loop frees the binding’s storage\n\nsawc/codegen/loops.py:168-197; sawc/typechecker/statements.py:4021-4036\n\nThe new checkpoint records a Copy transfer, but the sync loop still loads the head with _generate_expression and stores it without consuming the copy/retain decision before claiming cleanup ownership. Changing the new acceptance fixture’s static \"abc\" to interpolated \"abc {5}\" makes the full fixture segfault (exit -11). The reduced program below prints corrupted \"43 43\" on r2; exact base 82a6ab86 prints \"30 abc 5 0\". The static literal in the submitted fixture masks the freed heap storage. Consume the ordinary transfer decision at the actual iterator acquisition, not just in the checker.\n\n```saw\nstruct Words { text: String, index: Int }\nextension Words: Iterator {\n    type Item = Int\n    func next(&var self) -> Int? {\n        if self.index < self.text.len() {\n            self.index = self.index + 1\n            self.index\n        } else { None }\n    }\n}\nfunc walk(n: Int) sync {\n    let it = Words(text: \"abc {n}\", index: 0)\n    var total = 0\n    for x in it { total = total + x }\n    for x in it { total = total + x }\n    print(\"{total} {it.text} {it.index}\")\n}\nfunc main() { walk(5) }\n```\n\n2. [P1] Value-position for still bypasses the new NoCopy head checkpoint\n\nsawc/typechecker/statements.py:4084-4101; sawc/codegen/loops.py:350-383\n\nOnly _check_for_loop received the transfer checkpoint; _check_for_loop_as_expression did not. A named NoCopy iterator in `let got = for n in it { break n }` compiles and is destroyed twice. R2 output: \"drop counter / 7 / after loop / drop counter\"; exact base outputs \"7 / after loop / drop counter\". This is a wholly sync loop, not deferred SL-346’s spanning value-position case. Both statement and value forms acquire an owner and must enforce the same move/copy contract.\n\n```saw\nstruct Counter { index: Int }\nextension Counter: NoCopy {\n    func deinit(&var self) { print(\"drop counter\") }\n}\nextension Counter: Iterator {\n    type Item = Int\n    func next(&var self) -> Int? {\n        if self.index == 0 {\n            self.index = 1\n            7\n        } else { None }\n    }\n}\nfunc walk() sync {\n    let it = Counter(index: 0)\n    let got = for n in it { break n }\n    print(got ?? 0)\n    print(\"after loop\")\n}\nfunc main() { walk() }\n```\n\n3. [P1] A failing try behind ?? still forgets a later move that never ran\n\nsawc/coro_transform.py:2302-2312,2413-2441,7640-7647\n\n_ptry_stmt and _ptry skip conditional values. On the None path of `maybe ?? sink(try fail(), move r)`, fail() runs before move r, yet the whole-statement error landing still clears r. R2 prints \"4 / caught\", missing \"drop kept\"; exact base prints \"4 / drop kept / caught\". Decompose error sites within their guarded paths, without hoisting them outside their guards. This is a driven-body regression and is not SL-348’s pre-existing SYNC abandoned-argument issue.\n\n```saw\nimport std.task.{yield_now}\n\nstruct Res { name: String }\nextension Res: NoCopy {\n    func deinit(&var self) { print(\"drop {}\", self.name) }\n}\n\nstruct Bad { n: Int }\nextension Bad: Error {\n    func format(&self, into: &var StringBuilder) { try! into.append(\"bad\") }\n}\n\nfunc note(r: &Res) -> Int { r.name.len() }\nfunc fail() sync -> Result<Int, Bad> { Bad(n: 1) }\nfunc sink(n: Int, r: Res) sync -> Int { n }\n\nfunc work() -> Result<Int, Bad> {\n    var r = Res(name: \"kept\")\n    print(note(&r))\n    yield_now()\n    let maybe: Int? = None\n    let n = maybe ?? sink(try fail(), move r)\n    n\n}\n\nfunc main() {\n    match __saw_drive(work()) {\n        case Ok(n) -> print(n),\n        case Err(_) -> print(\"caught\")\n    }\n}\n```\n\n4. [P2] A propagating try inside a reference argument’s index produces invalid LLVM\n\nsawc/coro_transform.py:2452-2476,2562-2590,2730-2816\n\n`sink(&values[try fail_index()], move r)` fails compilation on r2 with LLVM’s `use of undefined value %caught_error` while exact base compiles and prints \"4 / drop kept / caught\". The new decomposition sees that the argument contains a try but its unconditional-child mapper has no ReferenceExpr descent; its place-index special handling applies only to a preceding reference sibling without a try. A borrowed place is not a value to hoist, but its evaluated indices still need position-preserving error decomposition. This is an observed compiler error, NOT a demonstrated runtime leak for this spelling.\n\n```saw\nimport std.task.{yield_now}\n\nstruct Res { name: String }\nextension Res: NoCopy {\n    func deinit(&var self) { print(\"drop {}\", self.name) }\n}\n\nstruct Bad { n: Int }\nextension Bad: Error {\n    func format(&self, into: &var StringBuilder) { try! into.append(\"bad\") }\n}\n\nfunc note(r: &Res) -> Int { r.name.len() }\nfunc fail_index() sync -> Result<Int, Bad> { Bad(n: 1) }\nfunc sink(value: &Int, r: Res) sync -> Int { 0 }\n\nfunc work() -> Result<Int, Bad> {\n    var r = Res(name: \"kept\")\n    print(note(&r))\n    let values: Vector<Int> = [9]\n    yield_now()\n    let n = sink(&values[try fail_index()], move r)\n    n\n}\n\nfunc main() {\n    match __saw_drive(work()) {\n        case Ok(n) -> print(n),\n        case Err(_) -> print(\"caught\")\n    }\n}\n```\n\n5. [P2] An alias-returning producer is certified without checking any returning path\n\nsawc/typechecker/borrowing.py:657-674\n\nThe producer check recognizes Alias as borrowing, but _producer_paths_missing_origin asks get_struct_info(ret.struct_name) before resolving the alias and returns success on None. The complete declaration below compiles even though bad returns only other.iter(), never a construction with lends self. Resolve the return type before proving its fields and paths; absence of struct information cannot mean origin proof succeeded. This finding is the missing declaration/origin check: attempts to drive this particular distinct alias are separately refused for lacking Iterator, so I am NOT claiming a demonstrated wrong-root runtime iteration.\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { value: Int }\nborrows struct It { source: &Owner, done: Bool }\ntype Alias = It\n\nextension Owner {\n    func iter(&self) borrows -> It {\n        It(source: lends self, done: false)\n    }\n    func bad(&self, other: &Owner) borrows -> Alias {\n        Alias(other.iter())\n    }\n}\n\nfunc main() {}\n```\n\n6. [P2] The borrowing-type fence misses aliases to composites and deeper compositions\n\nsawc/typechecker/borrowing.py:191-250\n\nThe new resolver follows aliases only when asking whether the whole type is a borrowing struct. _first_borrowing_struct_in then descends the original alias rather than its target. `Hidden = Vector<It>` therefore passes as a stored field and function parameter; the complete NoCopy Holder program below compiles. The same fence also accepts a Holder field with nine nested Vector wrappers because depth > 8 returns safe. Both programs were compiled successfully after giving Holder its independently required NoCopy policy. Resolve aliases before descending composition, and do not treat exhaustion of a traversal bound as evidence that a type contains no borrow.\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { value: Int }\nborrows struct It { source: &Owner, done: Bool }\ntype Hidden = Vector<It>\n\nstruct Holder {\n    value: Hidden\n}\n\nfunc accept(value: Hidden) -> Int { 0 }\nextension Holder: NoCopy {}\nfunc main() {}\n```\n\nThe independently verified depth-bound variant:\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { value: Int }\nborrows struct It { source: &Owner, done: Bool }\n\nstruct Holder {\n    value: Vector<Vector<Vector<Vector<Vector<Vector<Vector<Vector<Vector<It>>>>>>>>>\n}\n\nextension Holder: NoCopy {}\nfunc main() {}\n```\n\n7. [P2] The producer exemption still admits stored borrowing values and mutation of their origin\n\nsawc/typechecker/borrowing.py:281-294; sawc/typechecker/statements.py:2049-2063\n\nThe exemption applies to every bare borrowing-typed expression in a same-result producer, not only the construction/return being proved. The new binding hook only catches self. Below, bad stores other.iter() in held, mutates other while held remains live, reads 99 through held, and returns a valid self-origin construction. R2 compiles and prints \"99 / 1\". Reject the local binding: the enclosing method’s return type cannot exempt unrelated borrow values from the direct-head/window rule.\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { value: Int }\nborrows struct It { source: &Owner, done: Bool }\n\nextension Owner {\n    func iter(&self) borrows -> It {\n        It(source: lends self, done: false)\n    }\n    func bad(&self, other: &var Owner) borrows -> It {\n        var held = other.iter()\n        other.value = 99\n        print(held.next()!)\n        It(source: lends self, done: false)\n    }\n}\n\nextension It: Iterator {\n    type Item = Int\n    func next(&var self) -> Int? {\n        if self.done { None } else {\n            self.done = true\n            self.source.value\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfunc main() {\n    let root = Owner(value: 1)\n    var other = Owner(value: 2)\n    for x in root.bad(&var other) { print(x) }\n}\n```\n\n8. [P2] A local shadow of a module-static window root still falsely conflicts\n\nsawc/typechecker/borrowing.py:901-906,1022-1027; sawc/windows.py:341-345\n\nBoth root identity lookups consult only current_scope. The static ROOT therefore opens a window with no binding identity; an independent local ROOT constructed from its value is still compared by name. R2 rejects the local field assignment below as a write to the borrowed static. Renaming only the local binding and its uses to local compiles and prints 3; the window and static are unchanged. Resolve statics and locals to distinct stable identities before comparing projections.\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { value: Int }\nborrows struct It { source: &Owner, done: Bool }\n\nextension Owner {\n    func iter(&self) borrows -> It {\n        It(source: lends self, done: false)\n    }\n}\n\nextension It: Iterator {\n    type Item = Int\n    func next(&var self) -> Int? {\n        if self.done { None } else {\n            self.done = true\n            self.source.value\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nstatic ROOT: Owner = Owner(value: 1)\n\nfunc main() {\n    for n in ROOT.iter() {\n        var ROOT = Owner(value: ROOT.value + 1)\n        ROOT.value = ROOT.value + n\n        print(ROOT.value)\n    }\n}\n```\n\n9. [P2] The shared-field walk mistakes an unsafe pointer’s pointee for owner storage\n\nsawc/typechecker/borrowing.py:773-815; sawc/typechecker/statements.py:2223-2290\n\nThe new walk returns immediately on self.source, before checking whether a later pointer indirection leaves that referent’s storage. It rejects the unsafe pointee assignment below as a write through shared Owner. The ordinary `func poke(owner: &Owner) unsafe { owner.p[0] = 7 }` control compiles on r2; the existing immutable-lvalue walk explicitly stops at UnsafePointer indexing. Preserve that storage boundary: reading a pointer field does not make its independently pointed-to storage part of the shared Owner.\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { p: UnsafePointer<Int> }\nborrows struct It { source: &Owner, done: Bool }\n\nextension It {\n    func poke(&var self) unsafe {\n        self.source.p[0] = 7\n    }\n}\n\nfunc main() {}\n```\n\n10. [P2] Alias-spelled shared reference fields are falsely reported as having no lent place\n\nsawc/typechecker/types.py:956-994; sawc/typechecker/borrowing.py:657-663,801-807,840-848\n\n_borrowing_field_referent explicitly permits top-level aliases resolving to shared &T, but check_borrowing_struct_decl inspects the raw field kind. The legal declaration below is rejected with \"holds no lent place\". The producer proof, permission walk, and new codegen reference-field check likewise inspect raw field kinds, so accepting it only at the declaration would leave those consumers inconsistent. Use the resolved field category consistently. This is a false rejection, NOT a demonstrated permission bypass.\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { value: Int }\ntype OwnerRef = &Owner\n\nborrows struct It {\n    source: OwnerRef\n    done: Bool\n}\n\nfunc main() {}\n```\n\nVerification:\n- Exact patch applied in isolated .build/review-sl318p7-r2; no implementation edits or merge.\n- 16 r1 repros/controls rerun; intended corrected behavior observed in all.\n- Focused revised fixture suite: 58 passed, 1 known xfail (K141 / SL-340), 59 total.\n- tools/test_coro_shapes.py, tools/test_transfer_decisions.py, tools/test_producer_taxonomy.py, tools/test_window_seam.py: all exit 0.\n- Concrete new programs above compiled/executed; compile-only declaration checks are identified as such. Exact-base comparisons confirm the Copy corruption, value-for double destruction, conditional-try missing destruction, and reference-index LLVM failure are introduced by the patch.\n- Tracker currently says r2 tests pending, with tested_commit still 2781b4ce. Its attached full-suite output is therefore r1 evidence, not r2 validation.\n- Existing SL-340/341/345/346/348 remain separately scoped. No claim that the U3 patch completes epic SL-318.\n\nArtifacts: .build/sl318p7-r2-probes.json; .build/sl318p7-r2-suite.log; .build/sl318p7-r2-test_*.py.log; .build/review-sl318p7-r2/.build/scratch/review_*.saw. No implementation changes, commit, push, or merge performed.\n","created":"1790093090","id":"c81"},{"author":"agent:claude-sawlang","body":"LEAD ACK of codex r2 on SL-318.p7 (Sep 22): all ten accepted as filed; every one is an adjacent path of an r2 family and reads as three mechanisms. (F1) The head transfer is DECIDED but not CONSUMED: `_check_value_transfer` records the Copy/NoCopy answer for a `for` head, and codegen's iterator acquisition still loads the head bitwise before claiming cleanup ownership (#1 — a Copy-tier binding is freed by its first loop; codex's interpolated-String twin of the fixture segfaults), while the value-position lowering never asked the checkpoint at all (#2 — a NoCopy head in `let got = for n in it { break n }` is destroyed twice; a wholly sync loop, not SL-346's). The decision must be consumed at the acquisition, in the statement form, the value form and the driven twin. (F2) Positional relinquish stops at GUARDS and at PLACES: the leaf split skips conditional values, so `maybe ?? sink(try fail(), move r)`'s None path clears a move that never ran (#3), and it has no descent into a `ReferenceExpr`'s index, so `sink(&values[try fail_index()], move r)` emits `use of undefined value %caught_error` (#4) — the decomposition must descend into every guarded path WITHOUT hoisting an error site outside its guard, and into an index expression without hoisting the borrowed place. (F3) The borrowing rules resolve aliases LATE or NOT AT ALL, and two exemptions reach past their subject: the producer origin check asks `get_struct_info` on the alias name and treats \"no info\" as proof (#5); `_first_borrowing_struct_in` descends the alias rather than its target and a depth-bound exhaustion answers \"safe\" (#6 — `Hidden = Vector<It>` and nine nested `Vector`s both pass the fence); the producer exemption admits every bare borrowing-typed expression in the body rather than the value being PROVED, so `var held = other.iter()` inside a producer stores a borrow and mutates its origin (#7); the window root's identity lookups consult `current_scope` only, so a module static has no identity and a local shadow of its name conflicts by text (#8); the shared-field walk returns at the reference hop before an `UnsafePointer` indexing leaves the referent's storage, unlike `_immutable_lvalue_root` (#9); and an alias-spelled `&T` field is judged by its raw kind at the declaration while `_borrowing_field_referent` resolves it, so a legal field is refused and the consumers disagree (#10 — use ONE resolved field category everywhere).\n\nCodex's programs are staged in the worktree's `.build/scratch/lead/x_codex_r2_f<N>.saw` (#6 has an `a`/`b` pair). The lead reproduced both findings below on the exact submitted diff in an isolated checkout. The earlier r1/r2 findings are resolved in their reported shapes; these are adjacent gaps, not a re-report of the twenty original cases.\n\n1. [P1] Inline-catch normalization skips call arguments and tuple-backed aggregate slots\n\nsawc/coro_transform.py:3693-3723 (also _inline_catch_block at 3670-3691).\n\n_inline_catch_rewrite.visit stops at anything that is not an ASTNode. Argument is a plain dataclass, and struct field/map entries are tuples, so the walk never reaches an inline TryExpr inside those wrappers. Direct-let cases in K147 normalize correctly; these nested positions do not. In a spanning loop, a catch's raw break exits the coroutine dispatcher instead of the logical loop, silently skipping the code after the loop.\n\nMinimal sync/driven comparison:\n\n```saw\nimport std.task.{yield_now}\nstruct Bad { n: Int }\nextension Bad: Error {\n    func format(&self, into: &var StringBuilder) { try! into.append(\"bad\") }\n}\nfunc fail() sync -> Result<Int, Bad> { Bad(n: 1) }\nfunc id(n: Int) sync -> Int { n }\nfunc sync_work() sync {\n    var i = 0\n    while i < 2 {\n        let n = id(try fail() catch { break })\n        i = i + n\n    }\n    print(\"sync done {}\", i)\n}\nfunc driven_work() {\n    var i = 0\n    while i < 2 {\n        yield_now()\n        let n = id(try fail() catch { break })\n        i = i + n\n    }\n    print(\"driven done {}\", i)\n}\nfunc main() {\n    sync_work()\n    __saw_drive(driven_work())\n}\n```\n\nObserved independently by Sol and the lead: compile succeeds, runtime exits 0, output is only:\n\n```\nsync done 0\n```\n\nThe required `driven done 0` is missing. Sol also ran this on exact base 55436450 with the same result: this is pre-existing SL-215 behavior left unclosed by the patch's new normalization, NOT a regression introduced by r3. It is in the stated SL-215 fix scope. Sol's sibling with a suspending call in the argument's catch still receives the old Pending-SL-215 refusal; the equivalent block-form aggregate control prints 7. The direct-position K147 fixture passes.\n\nPlease traverse Argument and tuple-backed child positions through the existing child-position machinery while preserving the block/closure boundaries. Keep a nested-argument loop-exit regression beside the direct-position cases.\n\n2. [P2] The producer-return exemption admits composite borrowing types without checking them\n\nsawc/typechecker/borrowing.py:509-514 and 664-666.\n\n_borrowing_type_positions.returns_of exempts EVERY is_borrows declaration, but check_borrowing_producer only checks when the whole return type resolves to a bare borrowing struct. A composite return such as It? falls between the checks. The legal producer exception is for the bare borrowing-struct return, not arbitrary types containing it.\n\n```saw\nstruct Owner { value: Int }\nborrows struct It { source: &Owner, done: Bool }\nextension Owner {\n    func bad(&self) borrows -> It? { panic(\"never\") }\n}\nfunc main() {}\n```\n\nObserved independently by Sol and the lead: this compiles successfully. Removing only `borrows` gives the intended clean declaration error (`the return type of bad may not name a borrowing struct: It? ...`). Changing only `It?` to `Optional<It>` instead reaches `internal compiler error: Unknown generic struct: Optional`.\n\nThis is a declaration-contract/diagnostic hole in the new feature, not a demonstrated runtime escape: construction of an actual composite is separately refused by the expression fence. Narrow the exemption to the validated bare producer return and separately legal accessor forms; reject composites through reject_borrowing_type before codegen.\n\nVerification:\n- Sol reviewed the exact diff and the earlier reviews/fixes; no tracked implementation edits.\n- Sol compiled/exercised Copy-tier iterator acquisition, guarded try/move cleanup, borrowed-place index cleanup, alias/reference controls, direct inline catches, and the producer/composition/storage refusal fixtures. No prior finding remains in exactly its reported form. The r1 resolution assessment includes source inspection rather than a claim to rerun every original r1 reproducer.\n- Lead independently ran the focused test_runner selection under the suite lock: 68 passed, 1 expected failure (K141, SL-340). Both new repros plus the plain-return and Optional spelling controls were independently checked afterward.\n- Server revision-3 tests report 2636 passed / 10 expected failures and 36 freestanding passes across both targets. Neither Sol nor lead repeated the full terminal battery for this review.\n\nRequest changes on revision 3. No merge performed.\n","created":"1790110342","id":"c88"},{"author":"agent:claude-sawlang","body":"LEAD ACK of codex r3 on SL-318.p7 (Sep 22): both accepted as filed. #1 is the r2/r3 habit one more time — a walk that enumerates node shapes by hand where the child-position funnel already knows them: `_inline_catch_rewrite.visit` stops at anything that is not an `ASTNode`, so an inline `try … catch { break }` inside a call's `Argument`, a struct-literal field or a map entry is never normalized, its raw `break` leaves the resume dispatcher, and the code after the loop is silently skipped (pre-existing on the base; inside SL-215's stated scope, so it lands here). #2: `_borrowing_type_positions.returns_of` exempts EVERY `borrows` declaration's return while `check_borrowing_producer` proves only a BARE borrowing-struct return, so `borrows -> It?` falls between the two and `borrows -> Optional<It>` reaches an ICE; the exemption is narrowed to the validated bare producer return and the legal accessor forms, everything else goes through `reject_borrowing_type`.\n\nCodex's programs are staged as `.build/scratch/lead/x_codex_r3_f<N>.saw`. A place window may not span a suspension: the root\\n-  stays borrowed for the whole window, so yielding with one open would let\\n-  another task invalidate it. `with_ref` / `with_var_ref` remain the explicit\\n-  long-window and multi-statement spellings.\\n+- A `borrows` body is `sync`. An accessor's `lend` window may not span a\\n+  suspension, and neither may a `with_ref` / `with_var_ref` body: the root\\n+  stays borrowed for the whole window, and those two spellings record no extent\\n+  a reader could check it against. `with_ref` / `with_var_ref` remain the\\n+  explicit long-window and multi-statement spellings. The `for` window over a\\n+  borrowing struct is the one window that DOES span a suspension — see\\n+  *Borrowing structs* below, and *Suspension and the coroutine transform* for\\n+  what is known about it that is not known about these two.\\n - There are no `borrows` function *values* or existentials. A `borrows` method\\n   cannot be bound to a name or erased behind `any Trait`.\\n - Traits cannot require a `borrows` method. A generic `T: IndexPlace` bound is\\n   not part of this version.\\n \\n+#### Borrowing structs\\n+\\n+**Status: implemented.** A **borrowing struct** is a type that holds a lent\\n+place. It is declared `borrows struct`, one of its fields is a plain shared\\n+reference, and a `borrows` function returns one by value:\\n+\\n+```saw-fragment\\n+public borrows struct VectorIterator<T, A: Allocator = GlobalAllocator> {\\n+    private vector: &Vector<T, A>\\n+    private index: Int\\n+}\\n+\\n+extension Vector<T: Copy, A: Allocator = GlobalAllocator> {\\n+    public func iter(&self) borrows -> VectorIterator<T, A> {\\n+        VectorIterator<T, A>(vector: lends self, index: 0)\\n+    }\\n+}\\n+```\\n+\\n+Four spellings, one fact. The `borrows struct` keyword declares the type's\\n+nature where a reader meets the type; the `&Vector<T, A>` field is the\\n+ordinary reference spelling, and no second modifier restates it; `borrows` on\\n+a value-returning signature says at the declaration that the result borrows\\n+the receiver; and `lends self` at the initializer is the body's proof.\\n+\\n+**The window is the `for` statement.** A `borrows` call returning a borrowing\\n+struct is legal in exactly one position: the direct head of a `for` whose\\n+receiver is a place rooted in a named binding — a local, a parameter, `self`,\\n+or a field path of one. The window opens at the head's evaluation and closes\\n+when the statement ends, on every route out.\\n+\\n+```saw-fragment\\n+for x in v.iter() { total = total + x }   // the window's extent is this statement\\n+let it = v.iter()                          // error: a borrowing struct may not\\n+                                           // be bound by a `let`\\n+for x in make_vector().iter() { }          // error: bind the collection first —\\n+                                           // a temporary has no persistent\\n+                                           // storage for the window to point into\\n+```\\n+\\n+While the window is open the collection is borrowed shared, so the body may\\n+read it and may not grow it, replace it, move it or swap its elements. That is\\n+the same exclusivity error `v.push` already gets inside a `with_ref` window,\\n+and it is what makes iteration safe: before this rule an iterator held a raw\\n+buffer pointer and a length snapshot, so a body that pushed until the buffer\\n+reallocated read freed memory in safe code.\\n+\\n+**Nothing erases it.** A borrowing struct may not instantiate a type parameter\\n+— not `Optional<It>`, `Result<It, E>`, `Vector<It>`, `Box<It>` or a bare `T` —\\n+may not sit in a function type's return or parameters (`() -> It`,\\n+`(It) -> Int`, however deeply nested), may not be erased into an `any Trait`\\n+existential, and may not be a parameter, a struct field, a plain return type or\\n+an associated type. Each is refused at\\n+the declaration that names the type, so a helper that would forward one cannot\\n+be written rather than being caught at its call. It may conform to `Iterator`,\\n+which is how `for` reaches `next`, and only static dispatch reaches the\\n+conformance.\\n+\\n+**The origin is the receiver.** `lends self` is the only spelling, it requires\\n+a `&self` receiver, and every returning path must initialize every reference\\n+field with it. A projection (`lends self.buffer`), another reference parameter\\n+or a local names a root the call site cannot charge, and each is refused by\\n+name. The rule is why the iterator lends the vector rather than its buffer:\\n+`next()` reads `length` and `buffer` through the reference on every call, so\\n+nothing is snapshotted and there is no stale pointer to go stale.\\n+\\n+**Shared only.** A borrowing struct's reference fields are `&T`. A `&var`\\n+field is refused: an iterator holding `&var Vector<T>` could reallocate the\\n+collection another reader is walking through its own field, and recording the\\n+root would not catch it. Mutating the borrowing struct's own state is\\n+unaffected — `next(&var self)` advances its cursor, which is not mutable\\n+access to the borrowed collection.\\n+\\n+**Item is owned.** A borrowing struct's `Iterator.Item` may be neither a\\n+reference nor another borrowing struct, so the loop variable owns what it is\\n+handed. `Vector`'s `T: Copy` elements satisfy this.\\n+\\n+**Owned fields and `deinit` are supported**, and two things happen at the\\n+window's close in this order: the borrowing struct is destroyed, and then the\\n+root charge ends. The order is what lets a hand-written `deinit` read through\\n+the reference.\\n+\\n+A place is never a value outside a borrowing struct, and a borrowing struct is\\n+never a value outside its window.\\n+\\n #### Standard library accessors\\n \\n `Vector` and `Data` publish their element access as places:\\n@@ -7322,10 +7411,19 @@ Observable rules:\\n     spawned body needs none of that — it points into the task's own frame, which\\n     the box keeps alive. A `threads: N` group refuses a reference parameter\\n     outright, on `Send`.\\n-  - Container-internal borrows (`Vector.with_ref`/`with_var_ref`) keep their\\n-    `sync`-body restriction: unlike a confined stack/frame referent, a container\\n-    borrow projects into shared, reachable storage that a concurrent task could\\n-    reallocate across a suspension, so it may not span one.\\n+  - The `for` WINDOW spans a suspension; the closure and accessor spellings do\\n+    not. A `for x in v.iter()` head opens a tracked window over the collection\\n+    (see *Borrowing structs* under Places), and the window may hold across a\\n+    park because three things are known about it: its ORIGIN is recorded, its\\n+    EXTENT is the statement, and the Law of Exclusivity sees every competing\\n+    safe writer. A `&var` extent live at the head or started inside the body is\\n+    the writer-beside-reader error, a `&` extent composes, a `threads: N` group\\n+    refuses the frame on `Send` before the question arises, and nothing else in\\n+    this task runs while the frame is parked. `Vector.with_ref` /\\n+    `with_var_ref` bodies and `borrows` accessor `lend` windows RETAIN the\\n+    `sync` restriction: a suspension inside one is a compile error, and the\\n+    same argument would lift it, but it wants a consumer sweep and rows of its\\n+    own.\\n - **`deinit` may not suspend** — a `deinit` is always a `sync` context, so a\\n   suspension inside one is a compile error (deterministic destruction).\\n - **Effect polymorphism — generic suspending functions/methods** (design 70,\\n@@ -7571,10 +7669,31 @@ Observable rules:\\n       served\\n   }\\n   ```\\n+- **A suspension inside a `for` over a COLLECTION embeds.** The iterator becomes\\n+  frame state, the loop head re-enters through `next()`, and the split is the\\n+  one a `while let` already had: a spanning collection `for` is rewritten into\\n+  the loop it denotes, so `_split_while` and `_split_if_let` do the work and\\n+  there is no third routine. claim exactly ONCE — the same rule SL-234 gave the non-split `if`,\\n+// now reaching the SPLIT lowering too.\\n+//\\n+// THE TWO LOWERINGS, and why the rule had to be said twice. A `borrows`\\n+    function either `lend`s exactly once (design 141) or RETURNS a borrowing\\n+    struct, never both — `place_transform` splits on exactly that, by whether\\n+    the body contains a `lend`.\\n+(4) `lends self` at the init site is the body's proof, and THE ORIGIN IS A\\n+    CHECKED COMPILER FACT: U3 admits the RECEIVER and nothing else, the\\n+    receiver must be a REFERENCE receiver (`&self`), and the summary is\\n+    recorded on the declaration as `Method.borrow_origin` — a DECLARED\\n+    annotation field, so it rides `substitute_ast_types` through\\n+    monomorphization and travels with an imported declaration exactly as\\n+    `is_reference` does.\\n+\\n+THE FENCE, and the ONE REJECTOR (obligation 1). value positions\\n+    # ==================================================================== #\\n+\\n+    def check_borrowing_fence(self, expr, result) -> None:\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"THE FENCE, at It\\n+is not a for-loop feature: `for` is its FIRST CLIENT, and the reuse obligation\\n+(user, Sep 20) is that the generic scoped-borrow statement the follow-up brief\\n+specifies adds its syntax, its typechecking client and its acquisition/result\\n+binding — and NO second implementation of root accounting, pinning, suspension\\n+persistence or exit cleanup.\\n+\\n+WHY A RECORD AND NOT A RULE ON `ForLoop`. Three passes need the same four\\n+facts, and each of them would otherwise re-derive them from the loop's shape:\\n+\\n+  * the TYPECHECKER charges the root, refuses the writers, and accounts for\\n+    the close on every route;\\n+  * the COROUTINE TRANSFORM asks \\\"is a window live across this suspension\\\" and,\\n+    when it is, mints the frame field, encodes the referent as a design-88\\n+    pointer, and closes the window on every exit route out of the state\\n+    machine;\\n+  * CODEGEN lowers the sync form — the resource's slot, and the DROP-BEFORE-\\n+    CHARGE-END order.\\n+\\n+None of those three reads `ForLoop`. They read the RECORD, which is what makes\\n+the second client a new `open_window` call rather than a second copy of all\\n+three. (`tools/test_window_seam.py`, the `windowseam` battery lane, fails when\\n+a `ForLoop` mention appears in this module or in the transform's window\\n+handling outside the named adapter.)\\n+\\n+THE FOUR BOUNDARIES (codex c44), which this module's API shape encodes:\\n+\\n+  B1  ITERATION belongs to the client; WINDOW LIFETIME belongs here. The record\\n+      holds a GENERIC resource slot (`resource_name`, `resource_type`), never a\\n+      field named `__iter` nor an `Iterator`-shaped payload — the `for` client\\n+      puts an iterator in it, a future accessor client would put a lend result.\\n+      Not every `ForLoop` opens one: a RANGE loop and an OWNED-iterator loop\\n+      open none and take the ordinary split.\\n+  B2  A window closes by CONTROL-FLOW TARGET, not by the spelling of the exit.\\n+      `windows_left_by` takes a RESOLVED target and answers which windows an\\n+      edge leaves, inside-out. An implementation that special-cases `Continue`\\n+      as \\\"keep open\\\" leaks the first client's shape; this one asks whether the\\n+      target is inside or outside each extent.\\n+  B3  The record has a LIFECYCLE — ACQUIRE, ACTIVE, RELEASE — and RELEASE runs\\n+      a CLIENT-PROVIDED cleanup operation. For `for` that is \\\"destroy the\\n+      borrowing iterator\\\"; an accessor window's would be an epilogue, and an\\n+      optional head may take an `else` branch without ever activating a window,\\n+      so nothing here assumes release is a drop or that every evaluated head\\n+      opens a window.\\n+  B4  The direct-head / temporary-receiver refusals apply to BORROWING results\\n+      only. A window exists because a value CARRIES a borrow; a head that\\n+      produces an owned value opens none.\\n+\\n+THE MODES. `shared` is the only one U3 exercises; `exclusive` is reserved\\n+rather than invented, because the derivation (writer-versus-reader, nested\\n+windows) is the follow-up's to specify. The field is here so the follow-up\\n+adds rows rather than a second record.\\n+\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+\\n+from typing import Any, List, Optional, Tuple\\n+\\n+#: The window modes. `shared` composes with other readers; `exclusive` excludes\\n+#: everything. U3 opens shared windows only — see the module docstring.\\n+SHARED = 'shared'\\n+EXCLUSIVE = 'exclusive'\\n+MODES = (SHARED, EXCLUSIVE)\\n+\\n+#: The ORIGINS a window's borrow may have. U3 admits one, and the string is the\\n+#: summary recorded on the producing declaration (`Method.borrow_origin`), so\\n+#: the call site substitutes it onto the receiver place's root rather than\\n+#: walking the body.\\n+RECEIVER_ROOT = 'receiver root'\\n+ORIGINS = (RECEIVER_ROOT,)\\n+\\n+\\n+class StatementWindow:\\n+    \\\"\\\"\\\"ONE window: a root borrowed for the extent of one statement.\\n+\\n+    DELIBERATELY NOT A DATACLASS, and this is load-bearing rather than style.\\n+    The record is STAMPED ON THE STATEMENT (`ForLoop.window`), and\\n+    `typechecker/effects.py:substitute_ast_types` — monomorphization's type\\n+    rewrite — walks `dataclasses.fields()` rather than `structural_fields()`\\n+    and recurses into every dataclass VALUE it finds. A dataclass record whose\\n+    `extent` points back at the statement holding it is therefore a cycle, and\\n+    the walk goes down it until the interpreter's recursion limit. After the checker, `mono_copy` may clone\\n+    the statement and the clone's record still names the ORIGINAL node — which\\n+    costs nothing, because from the transform onward what is read is the root,\\n+    the mode and the resource, never the identity of the extent.\\n+\\n+    `root_path` is design 141's root attribution applied to the head's RECEIVER\\n+    place — `v.iter()` charges `('v', ())`, `st.patches.iter()` charges\\n+    `('st', ('patches',))`, an enclosing-owner path per design 8/10. It is what\\n+    every conflict question compares, and it is a PATH rather than a name\\n+    because a field path names a smaller thing than its owner and the Law\\n+    already knows how to overlap the two.\\n+\\n+    `extent` is the STATEMENT node the window lives for. Lexical, so every\\n+    route out leaves it — which is the whole of \\\"no route may leave the charge\\n+    live past the statement\\\".\\n+\\n+    `resource_*` is B1's generic slot: the value that CARRIES the borrow, which\\n+    the client initialized into persistent storage at ACQUIRE and which\\n+    RELEASE destroys before the charge ends.\\n+    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+    __slots__ = ('root_path', 'root_id', 'mode', 'origin', 'extent', 'client',\\n+                 'line', 'column', 'resource_name', 'resource_type', 'state',\\n+                 'reported')\\n+\\n+    def __init__(self, root_path, root_id, mode, origin, extent, client,\\n+                 line, column):\\n+        self.root_path: Tuple[str, Tuple[str, ...]] = root_path\\n+        self.root_id: Optional[int] = root_id\\n+        self.mode: str = mode\\n+        self.origin: str = origin\\n+        self.extent: Any = extent       # the statement node that IS the extent\\n+        self.client: str = client       # 'for' — supplies diagnostic wording\\n+        self.line: int = line\\n+        self.column: int = column\\n+        # B1's generic resource slot — the borrowing value, its type, and the\\n+        # name of the hidden binding it lives in (never nameable in source).\\n+        self.resource_name: Optional[str] = None\\n+        self.resource_type: Optional[Any] = None\\n+        # B3: ACQUIRE -> ACTIVE -> RELEASE. A window is only `active` once the\\n+        # resource is initialized into its slot; RELEASE never runs on an\\n+        # uninitialized resource, which is what an optional head's `else` arm\\n+        # needs and what a failing argument (A3) relies on.\\n+        self.state: str = 'acquiring'\\n+        # Lines already reported against, so one statement that reaches the\\n+        # root several times yields one diagnostic (the `_task_borrows`\\n+        # precedent).\\n+        self.reported: set = set()\\n+\\n+    @property\\n+    def root_name(self) -> str:\\n+        return self.root_path[0]\\n+\\n+    def renders_root(self) -> str:\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"The root as an author would read it back.\\n+\\n+        A path's projections are the Law of Exclusivity's own\\n+        `('field', name)` / `('tuple', i)` / `('index', k)` triples\\n+        (`_build_access_path`), so rendering is spelling them back rather than\\n+        joining strings.\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+        head, hops = self.root_path\\n+        out = head\\n+        for hop in hops or ():\\n+            if not isinstance(hop, tuple) or len(hop) != 2:\\n+                out += \\\".?\\\"\\n+            elif hop[0] == 'field':\\n+                out += f\\\".{hop[1]}\\\"\\n+            elif hop[0] == 'tuple':\\n+                out += f\\\".{hop[1]}\\\"\\n+            else:\\n+                out += \\\"[…]\\\"\\n+        return out\\n+\\n+\\n+#: An array index that is not a compile-time constant. Compared by IDENTITY,\\n+#: so it can never be equal to a real index value.\\n+DYNAMIC_INDEX = object()\\n+\\n+\\n+def paths_overlap(a: Tuple[str, Tuple[str, ...]],\\n+                  b: Tuple[str, Tuple[str, ...]]) -> bool:\\n+    \\\"\\\"\\\"Do two access paths name storage that can be the same?\\n+\\n+    THE ONE DEFINITION of the Law of Exclusivity's path algebra (obligation 1).\\n+    It lives in this leaf module because BOTH readers reach it here and neither\\n+    reaches the other: `typechecker/types.py:_paths_overlap` — the call-set,\\n+    task-borrow and place-window question — delegates to it, and `WindowTable`\\n+    asks it directly, because a window compares paths OUTSIDE any call.\\n+\\n+    THE TABLE. Different roots are disjoint. On the same root the hop sequences\\n+    are walked in parallel: different KINDS at one position, different field\\n+    names, different tuple indices or different CONSTANT array indices are\\n+    disjoint; a DYNAMIC index at a position overlaps whatever is there, because\\n+    the value is not known until run time; and running out of hops on either\\n+    side (one path a prefix of the other) is an overlap — `v` overlaps\\n+    `v.items`, `p.a` and `p.b` do not.\\n+\\n+    The dynamic-index row is the one a second implementation loses, and losing\\n+    it is unsound rather than merely conservative: the window's own copy\\n+    compared hops for EQUALITY, so `bins[i]` and `bins[0]` were judged disjoint\\n+    and a `bins[0].push` ran inside a window over `bins[i]` with `i == 0`\\n+    (codex r1 #3).\\n+    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+    if a[0] != b[0]:\\n+        return False\\n+    for ha, hb in zip(a[1] or (), b[1] or ()):\\n+        if not isinstance(ha, tuple) or not isinstance(hb, tuple):\\n+            return True                     # an unreadable hop is conservative\\n+        if ha[0] != hb[0]:\\n+            return False\\n+        if ha[0] == 'index':\\n+            if ha[1] is DYNAMIC_INDEX or hb[1] is DYNAMIC_INDEX:\\n+                continue\\n+            if ha[1] != hb[1]:\\n+                return False\\n+        elif ha[1] != hb[1]:\\n+            return False\\n+    return True\\n+\\n+\\n+class WindowTable:\\n+    \\\"\\\"\\\"THE ONE CHOKEPOINT every statement window is opened and closed through.\\n+\\n+    CLIENTS (obligation 1 — a funnel names its entries). Each client calls\\n+    `open_window` with its own root, mode, origin and extent, supplies its own\\n+    RELEASE operation, and reads back nothing of its own shape:\\n+\\n+      * `for` — `typechecker/borrowing.py:open_for_window` /\\n+        `close_for_window`, called from `typechecker/statements.py`'s two\\n+        `for` checkers. It supplies the head (a `borrows` producer call on a\\n+        place) and the body, and its release operation destroys the borrowing\\n+        iterator. THE ONLY CLIENT IN U3.\\n+\\n+      * (reserved) the generic scoped-borrow STATEMENT the follow-up brief\\n+        specifies — a keyword-introduced block binding a lent place, with an\\n+        `else` arm for a `borrows -> &T?` head. It would call `open_window`\\n+        with mode from its own spelling, an `else` arm that never reaches\\n+        `activate`, and a release operation that runs the accessor epilogue.\\n+\\n+    WHAT THE CHOKEPOINT DOES, so no client does it twice:\\n+      * the ROOT CHARGE (`open_window` -> `conflict_for`, read at the four\\n+        access sites the Law already has);\\n+      * the EXCLUSIVITY conflicts, including a `&var` extent live at the head\\n+        or STARTED inside the body;\\n+      * the MOVE / REASSIGN / TAKE / SWAP refusals on the root and on every\\n+        enclosing owner (K20's precedent, one message);\\n+      * the CLOSE-ON-EVERY-ROUTE accounting, by RESOLVED control-flow target\\n+        (`windows_left_by`).\\n+    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+\\n+    def __init__(self):\\n+        #: The open windows, OUTERMOST FIRST. LIFO: the innermost window is the\\n+        #: last entry, which is what makes `windows_left_by` answer inside-out\\n+        #: by walking the list backwards.\\n+        self.open: List[StatementWindow] = []\\n+        #: Every window this table ever opened, in open order — the transform\\n+        #: and codegen read records off their extent nodes, but the ledger is\\n+        #: what a dump and a gate lane enumerate.\\n+        self.all: List[StatementWindow] = []\\n+\\n+    # -- ACQUIRE / ACTIVE / RELEASE (B3) ---------------------------------\\n+\\n+    def open_window(self, root_path, root_id, mode, origin, extent, client,\\n+                    line, column) -> StatementWindow:\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"Open ONE window and make it the innermost. B3's ACQUIRE step A5.\\n+\\n+        The caller has already run A1-A4 — resolved the receiver PLACE, opened\\n+        the head's own shared borrow over the WHOLE call expression (arguments\\n+        included), evaluated the arguments left to right, and run the producer.\\n+        This is the HAND-OFF with no gap: the same root, the same mode, one\\n+        continuous extent.\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+        assert mode in MODES, mode\\n+        assert origin in ORIGINS, origin\\n+        w = StatementWindow(root_path=tuple(root_path), root_id=root_id,\\n+                            mode=mode, origin=origin, extent=extent,\\n+                            client=client, line=line, column=column)\\n+        self.open.append(w)\\n+        self.all.append(w)\\n+        return w\\n+\\n+    def activate(self, w: StatementWindow, resource_name, resource_type):\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"The resource is initialized into its persistent slot: ACTIVE.\\n+\\n+        Separated from `open_window` because RELEASE must never run on an\\n+        uninitialized resource — an optional head that takes its `else` arm,\\n+        and a head whose argument failed (A3), both leave a window that was\\n+        never activated and owes no cleanup.\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+        w.resource_name = resource_name\\n+        w.resource_type = resource_type\\n+        w.state = 'active'\\n+        return w\\n+\\n+    def close_window(self, w: StatementWindow):\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"RELEASE. Exactly once, and only on a window that is open.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+        if w in self.open:\\n+            self.open.remove(w)\\n+        w.state = 'released'\\n+        return w\\n+\\n+    # -- B2: closing by CONTROL-FLOW TARGET ------------------------------\\n+\\n+    def windows_left_by(self, target_extents) -> List[StatementWindow]:\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"The open windows an edge LEAVES, innermost first.\\n+\\n+        `target_extents` is the set of extent nodes the edge's RESOLVED target\\n+        is still inside — everything the edge does NOT leave. A window whose\\n+        extent is in that set stays open; every other open window closes, and\\n+        they close inside-out.\\n+\\n+        This is B2 stated as one question rather than as a case per statement\\n+        kind. `continue` targeting THIS loop passes the loop's own extent, so\\n+        the window stays; `break` targeting it does not, so it closes;\\n+        `break`/`continue` targeting an INNER loop passes every outer extent,\\n+        so nothing of the outer closes; a window nested inside an outer loop\\n+        closes when control continues that outer loop, because the outer loop's\\n+        extent is in the set and the inner one is not; and `return`, an error\\n+        propagation and a cancellation pass the EMPTY set, so every crossed\\n+        scope closes.\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+        keep = {id(e) for e in (target_extents or ())}\\n+        return [w for w in reversed(self.open) if id(w.extent) not in keep]\\n+\\n+    # -- the root charge, read by the Law's existing access sites ---------\\n+\\n+    def conflict_for(self, root_path, writes: bool,\\n+                     started_inside: bool = False,\\n+                     root_id: Optional[int] = None) -> Optional[StatementWindow]:\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"The innermost open window an access to `root_path` collides with.\\n+\\n+        IDENTITY FIRST, PROJECTIONS SECOND. A window borrows a BINDING; the\\n+        path only carries the name it was spelled with. Where the caller can\\n+        resolve the access's current binding and the window recorded its own,\\n+        two different bindings never conflict however alike they read — which\\n+        is what makes a legal refining shadow inside the body\\n+        (`var v = v.copy()`) an independent root. Either side unknown falls\\n+        through to the path comparison, which is the conservative answer.\\n+\\n+        THE TABLE, which is the Law of Exclusivity read over a statement-length\\n+        window rather than a call-length one:\\n+\\n+          * a SHARED window composes with other readers and collides with a\\n+            WRITE, a MOVE, a REASSIGN, a TAKE or a SWAP of the root or of any\\n+            enclosing owner on its path;\\n+          * an EXCLUSIVE window (reserved) collides with every touch.\\n+\\n+        `started_inside` names an access that OPENS a new by-reference extent\\n+        inside the body (a `&var` argument, a design-189 task capture): those\\n+        conflict on the same table, and the flag exists only so the diagnostic\\n+        can say which of the two the author wrote.\\n+        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+        for w in reversed(self.open):\\n+            if w.state == 'released':\\n+                continue\\n+            if (root_id is not None and w.root_id is not None\\n+                    and root_id != w.root_id):\\n+                continue                    # a different BINDING of one name\\n+            if not paths_overlap(w.root_path, tuple(root_path)):\\n+                continue\\n+            if w.mode == EXCLUSIVE or writes:\\n+                return w\\n+        return None\\ndiff --git a/tools/battery.sh b/tools/battery.sh\\nindex 6e44296c..b9e04c9a 100755\\n--- a/tools/battery.sh\\n+++ b/tools/battery.sh\\n@@ -67,6 +67,7 @@ STAGES=(\\n     \\\"producertaxonomy|no|every value-position node says how it produces a value|$PY tools/test_producer_taxonomy.py\\\"\\n     \\\"corodiscovery|no|one ledger answers every coroutine frame decision|$PY tools/test_coro_discovery.py\\\"\\n     \\\"corototality|no|every shape a suspension sits in SPLITs, HOISTs, INLINEs, EMBEDs or REFUSEs|$PY tools/test_coro_shapes.py\\\"\\n+    \\\"windowseam|no|the statement window is a structure, not a for-loop feature|$PY tools/test_window_seam.py\\\"\\n     \\\"stdseed|no|a cached std seed key names the METHOD ITS ENTRY IS ABOUT|$PY tools/test_std_seed_keying.py\\\"\\n     \\\"citations|no|the files nothing compiles: stale DF/SL citations, committed conflict markers|$PY tools/check_citations.py\\\"\\n     \\\"forgetgate|no|every __saw_forget and M1/M3 stamp cites its deferral|$PY tools/test_forget_purge.py\\\"\\ndiff --git a/tools/test_coro_shapes.py b/tools/test_coro_shapes.py\\nindex 33051705..f1cbe472 100644\\n--- a/tools/test_coro_shapes.py\\n+++ b/tools/test_coro_shapes.py\\n@@ -53,6 +53,7 @@ pass vacuously.\\n \\n import ast\\n import os\\n+import re\\n import subprocess\\n import sys\\n \\n@@ -175,14 +176,24 @@ def check_rows_are_well_formed():\\n                     f\\\"because the split does not exist YET must point at the \\\"\\n                     f\\\"work that would build it, or the refusal is a dead end.\\\")\\n         if row.disposition == coro_shapes.SPLIT:\\n-            if not row.handler.startswith(\\\"_split_\\\"):\\n+            # it denotes, so `_split_while` and `_split_if_let` do the work and\\n+            # a normalization runs ahead of them. A grep a human runs once is a claim that\\n+rots the next time somebody reaches for `stmt.variable` inside the common layer,\\n+which is exactly how a \\\"generic\\\" mechanism becomes its first client's. So it is\\n+a lane.\\n+\\n+WHAT IT CHECKS, and why each one is the thing that would go wrong:\\n+\\n+  1. `sawc/windows.py` — the record and the chokepoint — names no AST class and\\n+     no iteration vocabulary in its CODE. Prose may discuss `ForLoop`; the\\n+     module must not import or touch one.
